hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- the whole 75-row aligned raw view was read (`python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/enemy/critter CritterLineNodeColSub --diff --raw`) and the six differing words are exactly the three defining instructions at 0x18/0x1c/0x20 and their three uses at 0xa8 (`fadds f0,f30,f0` vs `f29`), 0xb4 (`fcmpo cr0,f31,f29` vs `f30,f31`) and 0xd4 (`fcmpo cr0,f0,f31` vs `f0,f30`). Every other row is `=`. NOT screened: the f64-width lever, because no count-neutral spelling of it exists (an f32 local emits lfs, not lfd).
hypothesis.statement: The residual is a CLASS-ORDER inversion between MWCC's f64-local FPR class and its f32-parameter FPR class, not an ordering fact inside either class, and the next lane should attack the CLASS membership of `zero` rather than its position. Emission order is IDENTICAL in both streams (0x18 `fmr fX,f1` = radius, 0x1c `lfd fX,lbl_80346550` = zero, 0x20 `fmr fX,f2` = dotThreshold); only the numbering permutes. Target numbers (f29,f30,f31) = (zero, radius, dotThreshold) -- the f64 constant LAST, i.e. lowest; ours numbers them (radius, dotThreshold, zero) -- the f64 constant FIRST, i.e. highest. Because A1's within-block reorder was NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, the two are in different allocator classes and claim.law.MV_callee-saved-numbering-has-a-width-class-ahead-of-declaration-order.20260902.v1's corollary applies verbatim: a cross-class reorder is byte-identical and proves the boundary rather than moving it. The one untried lever that changes CLASS rather than position is the local's WIDTH -- but `lfd` requires an f64 and an f32 spelling emits `lfs`, so the count-neutral version of that lever does not exist here, which is why this record caps rather than queues it.
